trust_center.repositoryDescription: Specset Trust Center, the single repository for FedRAMP Certification Data for the Specset Cloud Platform. The landing page, compliance posture summary, subprocessor list and FAQ are public. Specset's dated progress toward FedRAMP Certification (MKT-IIP-DCP) is published at https://www.specset.com/security#fedramp-progress. The Class A certification data has been published there since 2026-09-14 as restricted resources, with no non-disclosure agreement or acceptance of terms required. FedRAMP certified the offering at 20x Class A on 2026-11-06, and FedRAMP's Certification Report has been there since that day. Twenty-five are open to access requests; the documentation list here names each document. The two SOC 2 engagement letters and the management representation letter are private, supplied on request to fedramp@specset.com.
trust_center.accessRequestInstructions: The landing page at https://trust.specset.com requires no login. FedRAMP staff and agency reviewers request access to the restricted FedRAMP Certification Data from the Trust Center page. Requests from fedramp.gov and gsa.gov email addresses are approved automatically; Specset approves all other requests manually. Specset does not require acceptance of terms or a non-disclosure agreement. If a request is not approved within one business day, email fedramp@specset.com.

secure_configuration_guidance.repositoryDescription: Specset's Secure Configuration Guide (SCG-CSO-RSC), a public page in the product documentation written for the administrators of a customer organization: the roles that control an organization and the FedRAMP term for each, the recommended security settings for an organization that holds federal information or CUI and what each does, how Admin accounts are set up, reviewed and removed, and how account access is requested and recovered. It gives the recommended settings in JSON with the API query that exports an organization's current settings for comparison, and the version history of the recommended settings.

certified_services.serviceDescription: The offering as a whole: one multi-tenant SaaS service for construction document intelligence, used in a web browser on a computer or phone. An organization's members keep the project record in it (project manuals and specifications, drawing sets, submittals, RFIs, daily logs and photos, issues and documents), and every feature listed below runs on that record inside the same boundary. Production runs on Google Cloud in project specset-prod-assured (Assured Workloads, FEDRAMP_MODERATE control package, us-west1), with the supporting services listed under third-party information resources. Security category: Moderate (FIPS 199), reflecting the Controlled Unclassified Information the service handles for defense and federal customers. The whole service carries that one category, and no feature carries a different one. A per-organization CUI mode keeps model, embedding and web-grounding calls in the Assured Workloads project (Vertex AI, location us), turns off the commercial AI and support-chat integrations and the Procore and Autodesk integrations, and never calls Perplexity. Federal tenants are provisioned with CUI mode enabled.
Plain-language questions from anywhere in a project, answered from the project's own documents with a citation to each source.
Reviews specifications and drawings in project-wide context and returns conflicts, omissions and constructability risks, each cited to its source.
Reviews submittal packages (mix designs, shop drawings, product data, safety plans and more) against the applicable project requirements and returns the package annotated.
Compares two plan sets, or two revisions of one sheet, and returns each change matched by sheet and classified by what it touches.
Drafts documents such as safety plans, quality-control plans, closeout forms and proposal sections from the project record into the customer's own Word template.
Tracks each RFI against the conformed specifications and current drawings, and checks the answer before it reaches the field.
Reads the project manual and builds a cited register of the product data, samples, shop drawings and closeout packages it requires.
Merges the base specification, every addendum and the special provisions into one conformed text per section, searchable and cited to the paragraph.

Extracts opportunities from bid boards and notices and reads the invitation for damages, bonding, set-asides and schedule risks. Reading a public bid-portal page uses Firecrawl, listed under third-party information resources; organizations in CUI mode are not offered it.
Works the agreement, conditions and special provisions through a checklist and returns a severity-flagged review table.
Imports a Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project schedule, computes the network and answers questions about what slipped, what drives the finish and what comes next.

Turns the specifications, equipment schedules, submittals and O&M package into a structured facility record of assets, warranties and maintenance schedules, which the owner's team uses through the F&M portal after handoff.
Lets an organization write down its own procedure (a checklist, an extraction or a deliverable in its template) for the agents to run on every project.

certified_services.serviceName: Specset API, command-line tool and AI-assistant connectors
certified_services.serviceDescription: The Specset API, the specset command-line tool, and the connector (MCP) through which a member uses Specset from Claude, ChatGPT or Codex. Each acts with the member's own sign-in and permissions. The API and the connector endpoint run inside the service; the assistant a member connects is not part of the offering (see Not included).

certified_services.serviceName: Procore and Autodesk Construction Cloud integrations
certified_services.serviceDescription: Optional, customer-initiated connections to the customer's own Procore or Autodesk tenant through OAuth, moving only the records the customer chooses. Not available to an organization in CUI mode: an application gate stops it from connecting either integration and makes an existing connection inert.

certified.useCase: Google Cloud Platform (Google Services) — primary hosting of all production infrastructure in project specset-prod-assured (Assured Workloads): GKE Autopilot, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Memorystore, Cloud KMS, Cloud Load Balancing and Cloud Armor, Cloud Logging and Monitoring, Secret Manager, Artifact Registry, and Vertex AI (Gemini) model inference, embeddings and Web Grounding for Enterprise. Organizations in CUI mode use Vertex AI in the Assured Workloads project at location us only; other organizations use Vertex AI in a peer Google Cloud project, specbook-production, outside Assured Workloads. Stores and processes customer data. A third Google Cloud project, specbook-development, holds the development user-content buckets, development service identity and development vendor-key secrets; it sits outside Assured Workloads and inside the assessment scope because it shares integration credentials and software delivery with production. It does not handle federal customer data. A founder-run project-clone tool is built to copy a production project into the founder's local development environment on their laptop for debugging, not into this project (a full clone does not check that its object store is local), so a founder's laptop may hold customer content of organizations not in CUI mode. Specset enables CUI mode on any tenant provisioned for a federal customer before federal content is uploaded; the clone tool refuses any organization in CUI mode, for a full clone since 2026-10-12 and for a re-copy of an already-cloned project's files since 2026-10-13, and no organization now in CUI mode has been cloned. Two further Google Cloud projects are inside the assessment scope and hold no customer content: specset-dataroom, an investor data room with no connection to the offering, and vanta-scanner, which holds the compliance scanner's federated identity and read-only custom roles outside the boundary project.

AWS US East/West — supporting services: Amazon SES (outbound transactional email and, since 2026-10-29, email received for project addresses), Route 53 (DNS), S3 (CI build cache, CloudTrail audit logs, a legacy database-backup bucket from the pre-2026 hosting platform, and received email), SQS (received-email notifications), GuardDuty (threat detection), and Amazon Bedrock (Claude model inference entered in us-west-2 through global cross-Region inference profiles, which may process requests in any AWS commercial Region; for organizations not in CUI mode only; prompts may include customer document text). For an organization not in CUI mode, notification bodies may carry project content, and a submittal-review notification attaches the marked-up review PDF (on unless the project turns it off) and the review spreadsheet (off unless the project turns it on). Since 2026-10-21 05:32 UTC an organization in CUI mode receives, in place of each notification that can carry project content, a notice with a link and no project content or attachment; the link resolves only for an authenticated member of the organization. Since 2026-10-29 Amazon SES also receives email for project addresses (projects.specset.com): SES accepts the message outside the boundary, scans it, writes it to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket in the same account and notifies an encrypted SQS queue, and the workers read the queue and the object and delete them. Project addresses are only for organizations with the project email feature and never for organizations in CUI mode; no organization has the feature as of 2026-10-30, and the bucket deletes a message after four days.

Azure Commercial Cloud — Azure OpenAI (GPT model inference for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text), Microsoft Entra ID application registrations for customer 'Sign in with Microsoft' single sign-on, and a Windows evaluation lab in the same subscription, whose runbook allows public or synthetic files only (not technically enforced).

Google Workspace — provider identity (Cloud Identity) for staff access to production through Identity-Aware Proxy, with security-key or passkey 2-Step Verification enforced for all staff; staff email including the FedRAMP Security Inbox. No customer data.

GitHub Enterprise Cloud — source control and CI/CD for the application and infrastructure-as-code. Dependabot security alerts and CodeQL code scanning run on the application and infrastructure repositories, with Dependabot version updates on the infrastructure repository. Deploys to production through OpenID Connect workload identity federation. GitHub also hosts the marketing website repository, whose continuous integration publishes the website and the public copy of this document; Dependabot runs on it, and the website publisher can write only the website bucket. No customer data.

Vanta Trust Management Platform — continuous configuration monitoring of the production cloud accounts (read-only metadata), compliance evidence and policies, and the Specset Trust Center at trust.specset.com. Since 2026-10-29 its scanner holds, on the boundary project, custom roles with the permissions of Google's Security Reviewer role except those that list log entries, Data Access audit-log entries and bucket objects. Until then it held that role, which also let it read the boundary project's Data Access audit-log entries and list object names, both of which identify customer documents; whether Vanta read them is not known.

Slack — operational alerting and change-notification channel for the provider (infrastructure change notifications, security alerts), and delivery of prospect inquiries from the public website's contact form. Resource metadata and prospect contact details only; no customer content or customer-user data.

Perplexity Enterprise and API Platform (FedRAMP Certified, Class B) — web search for AI features of organizations not in CUI mode. Receives model-generated search queries; customer documents are not sent. Never called for organizations in CUI mode: their web lookups run on Vertex AI Web Grounding for Enterprise inside the Google Cloud Assured Workloads project.

nonCertified.name: Anthropic API (Claude, direct)
nonCertified.useCase: Direct Claude model inference for a small set of models not served through Amazon Bedrock, selectable only by Specset administrators; prompts may include customer document text. Never enabled for organizations in CUI mode. Retired on 2026-11-05: the application no longer calls this API and its egress allowance is removed, so no information flow reaches it; the entry stays until the information-resources inventory edition that retires the record.

nonCertified.name: Intercom
nonCertified.useCase: In-app customer support chat for organizations not in CUI mode. Processes customer user contact details and support conversation content; no project documents. The messenger never loads for an organization in CUI mode and its memberships are never shared with Intercom.

nonCertified.name: Google Generative AI (AI Studio)
nonCertified.useCase: Gemini API path outside the Google Cloud FedRAMP boundary, used as the embedding provider for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text. Never used for organizations in CUI mode, whose embeddings run on Vertex AI in the Assured Workloads project. Retirement is planned before the Class C application.

nonCertified.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
nonCertified.useCase: Cloudflare AI Gateway and Workers AI for experimental open-model inference selectable by organizations not in CUI mode. Prompts may include customer document text, and inference runs in Cloudflare data centers worldwide. The gateway does not store prompt or completion payloads, and the per-organization CUI mode excludes it. Cloudflare also supplies the edge fronting for the Trust Center custom hostname (trust.specset.com) as part of Vanta's Trust Center service; that use carries no customer data. The Cloudflare for Government offering is not used.

nonCertified.name: NOAA / National Weather Service APIs
nonCertified.provider: US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (federal agency)
nonCertified.useCase: Public weather and tide data for project daily logs. Receives a project site's latitude and longitude only; forecasts and tide data are returned to the daily log. Nothing is stored at the service. A US federal government data service, not a cloud service offering.

nonCertified.name: Apryse
nonCertified.provider: Apryse Software Inc. (formerly PDFTron Systems Inc.)
nonCertified.useCase: Document-processing software from one vendor, used two ways, both inside the boundary or in the user's browser. The server-side PDF library runs in the application and worker pods on customer documents, and the structured-output module it needs is downloaded from the vendor at container image build and pinned by SHA-256 checksum. The browser viewer runs under an offline OEM license key, so viewing makes no call to the vendor. No customer document data is sent to the vendor; the resource is in scope as a software-supply-chain dependency that affects document-processing availability and build integrity.

nonCertified.name: Autodesk Platform Services
nonCertified.useCase: Optional customer-initiated integration to the customer's own Autodesk tenant through OAuth; the customer chooses and authorizes the data exchanged. Not used unless a customer connects it. Disabled for organizations in CUI mode: an application gate, deployed 2026-09-13, stops an organization in CUI mode from connecting the integration and makes an existing connection inert.

nonCertified.name: Procore
nonCertified.useCase: Optional customer-initiated integration to the customer's own Procore tenant through OAuth; the customer chooses and authorizes the data exchanged. Not used unless a customer connects it. Disabled for organizations in CUI mode: an application gate, deployed 2026-09-13, stops an organization in CUI mode from connecting the integration and makes an existing connection inert.

nonCertified.name: Claude Code (Anthropic) — engineering assistant
nonCertified.useCase: Coding assistant run on operator laptops by the two technical founders and, since 2026-10-23, a developer. It is in the assessment scope because what it reads is sent to the model provider and can include federal customer data. It acts with the operator's own access, and the operator is responsible for what it reads; as a developer, a person may mint only the read-only service account's tokens and holds no other Google Cloud access to production. Specset's rule since 2026-10-09 is that data of organizations in CUI mode must not reach an engineering assistant, and the tooling keeps its default reads inside that rule. Infrastructure reads go through a dedicated read-only service account with reader roles only, no secret values and no write permission on production; since 2026-10-10 it cannot read the database rows of organizations in CUI mode, credential tables or Data Access audit logs, and it sees those organizations' application log entries only as sanitized copies. Database rows are read through a time-limited tunnel whose start the person running the assistant approves each session, the same founder or developer, not a second person, with Cloud SQL IAM authentication and SELECT-only grants. Every tunnel start is recorded as an Admin Activity audit entry, and an alert fires if the account ever appears as the principal of a write.

nonCertified.name: OpenAI Codex — engineering assistant
nonCertified.useCase: Coding assistant run on operator laptops by the two technical founders and, since 2026-10-23, a developer, in the assessment scope on the same terms as Claude Code. It acts with the operator's own access, under the operator's responsibility for what it reads and the rule that data of organizations in CUI mode must not reach an engineering assistant. It reads the infrastructure as the same read-only service account, which has no write permission on production, and reads database rows through the same SELECT-only, time-limited tunnel, whose start the person running it approves. Every tunnel start is recorded as an Admin Activity audit entry, and an alert fires on any write by that account. What it reads is sent to the model provider.

nonCertified.name: Cursor (Anysphere) — coding agent
nonCertified.useCase: Coding agent. Its GitHub App, installed on the marketing website repository only, has read that site's source and proposed changes to it since 2026-09-29; since 2026-10-23 a developer also uses its local agent on the application and infrastructure source. Model inference runs through Cursor's service. It was outside the assessment scope while it reached only the marketing website, and is in it since the local agent began, because its edits affect software integrity and because a script it writes could use the developer's own credentials. Specset's rule is that it works on code only and reads no customer data, and a fail-closed hook in the application and infrastructure repositories refuses the known paths to production, customer data and credentials; what the developer's credentials reach is bounded by Google Cloud IAM (no production access beyond minting the read-only service account's tokens, and no grant on customer documents) and by the application. Changes reach the application, the infrastructure and www.specset.com only through pull requests that a founder approves under each repository's branch protection.

nonCertified.name: Firecrawl
nonCertified.useCase: Two dependencies on one vendor. The hosted scraper reads public bid-portal pages for specification research and receives the page URL together with the extraction instructions the assistant's model wrote, which may derive from a user's conversation; no document, embedding or database row is sent. The vendor's PDF parser is a pinned software dependency that runs inside the boundary on customer PDFs, so no customer document reaches the vendor through it. Since 2026-10-21 the hosted scraper refuses an organization in CUI mode; until then such an organization could reach it.

nonCertified.name: Customer single sign-on identity providers (Google Sign-In and customer-configured OpenID Connect providers)
nonCertified.provider: The customer's own identity provider (Google Sign-In, or any OpenID Connect provider a customer configures)
nonCertified.useCase: Customer-chosen authentication for customer users. Specset receives the identity assertion and the claims the customer's provider releases; no project document or row leaves the boundary. Each provider is the customer's own information resource under the customer's own administration, so its certification status is the customer's decision. Corporate Google single sign-on is enforced for Specset staff and superadmin access.

current.service_desc: The Specset Cloud Platform is an AI platform for construction document review. It automates technical review across project manuals, drawing sheets and shop drawings: submittal review against project specifications, UFGS (Unified Facilities Guide Specifications) compliance checking, design review automation, asset management logic, and search and question answering across a project's documents. The platform flags potential issues and returns cited answers drawn from the customer's own project documents. Specset is the trade name of Spot.xyz Corporation, formerly Specbook. The SOC 2 Type II report supporting this package is issued to Spot.xyz Corporation DBA Specset, and the Unique Entity Identifier above is registered to that entity. FedRAMP ID FR2631258135 is the only Marketplace listing for this offering; the duplicate created at intake, FR2631747321, is no longer listed.
